stem: Which child best fits the criterion for considering short stature secondary to being born small for gestational age with no catch-up growth?

options.text: A 2-year-old with height below the 2nd centile
A 5-year-old with height below the 2nd centile and birth weight below the 2nd centile
A 5-year-old with normal height and low birth weight
A 5-year-old with height below the 2nd centile but normal birth measurements
A 10-year-old with delayed bone age only

explanation: A 5-year-old with height below the 2nd centile and birth weight below the 2nd centile is the correct answer because this fits the criterion of short stature in a child older than 4 years who was born small for gestational age and has not shown catch-up growth.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Assessment of Childhood Short Stature

rationale: The criterion requires both current short stature and a history of low birth size, and it applies after 4 years of age.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the criterion applies to children older than 4 years.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because this child is older than 4 years, has height below the 2nd centile, and had birth weight below the 2nd centile, which fits the SGA no catch-up growth criterion.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because normal current height does not meet the short stature criterion.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because low birth measurements are required as part of the criterion.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because delayed bone age alone suggests a different pattern and does not meet the SGA criterion.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
